newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mexico's Zedillo sees 1997 GDP growth at 4.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Zedillo sees 1997 GDP growth at 4.5 pct.

text.p: Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo said on Tuesday that he expected his country's gross domestic product to grow 4.5 percent in 1997.
"Economic recovery will be consolidated in 1997. We are looking at a GDP growth of 4.5 percent, inflation as close as possible to 15 percent," Zedillo told reporters in Tokyo.
"Our economic programme will look at 1997 as a transition period to a period of sustained growth of at least five percent GDP growth from 1998 onwards," he said.

Zedillo said that in 1996, the economy grew a little over five percent, and inflation, although still high, was reduced to almost half its previous rate. He added that financial markets, including the peso-dollar exchange rate, have shown remarkable stability.
"Our annual average export growth over the past 10 years has been greater than developed nations such as Germany and the U.S., and even greater than most 'Asian Tigers'," he said.

Last month, Mexican financial markets surged after the release of a surprisingly strong GDP growth of 5.1 percent for 1996. In the fourth quarter of the year, it rose by 7.6 percent from the same period a year earlier.
Zedillo is on an official visit to Japan, which ends Friday. He leaves for the western Japanese cities of Osaka and Kyoto on Wednesday.
